verdict: Symbotic grew revenue 22% to $721M and swung to a $55M net profit, helped by $31M of other income — though $43M of that profit belongs to its joint-venture partners, leaving $12M for shareholders.

kpis.label: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.note: The company's cash-style profit measure — more than double the $45M a year ago

kpis.label: Cash
kpis.note: Cash and equivalents at June 27, down from $2.0B in Q2 as projects ramped; Q4 revenue guided to $760–780M

segments.name: Systems
segments.note: Building and installing the automated warehouse systems — robots, storage and software — mostly for Walmart and other large distributors. Up 20% YoY.

segments.name: Operation services
segments.note: Running customers' automated warehouses day to day. Up 49% YoY.

segments.name: Software maintenance & support
segments.note: Keeping the warehouse software updated and supported. Up 57% YoY.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Improving the robots and warehouse software. Down 12% YoY on a GAAP basis.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling plus the back office, including stock pay. Up 18% YoY.

otherDetail: Net $21.0M was added outside operations: $30.6M of other income — mainly fair-value gains on strategic investments after observable price changes, plus interest and dividend income — less a $9.6M loss from an equity-method investment (a stake whose profits and losses Symbotic shares). The tax line was a $1.1M benefit.

follow100.label: Other income, net of equity loss

follow100Note: The $55M net profit is the whole company's, including partners' shares: $43.3M of it is attributable to noncontrolling interests (partners in Symbotic's joint ventures), leaving $11.7M — about $1.62 of every $100 of revenue — attributable to Symbotic's own shareholders.

takeaways.title: Growth held up, profit arrived
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 22% to $721M, almost all of it warehouse systems ($671M). Gross margin widened to 22% from 19% a year ago, and the company swung from a $26M operating loss to a $33M operating profit. It had 77 systems in deployment and guided Q4 revenue to $760–780M.

takeaways.title: Other income did heavy lifting
takeaways.text: On top of operating profit came $30.6M of other income, mainly paper gains from marking strategic investments to new observable prices, less a $9.6M equity-method loss and plus a $1.1M tax benefit. That is how a $33M operating profit became a $55M net profit — investment gains, not warehouse work, supplied much of the jump.

takeaways.title: Shareholders' slice is the smaller one
takeaways.text: Of the $55M net income, $43.3M is attributable to noncontrolling interests — partners who co-own parts of the business, chiefly through the Walmart-related joint venture — leaving $11.7M for Symbotic shareholders, or $0.09 per diluted share. Adjusted EBITDA, the measure management steers by, more than doubled to $95M.

oneTimers: Other income includes fair-value gains on strategic investments driven by observable price changes in the quarter (the 10-Q attributes most of the $22M YoY increase in other income to these adjustments) — paper gains that can reverse.
Restructuring charges were zero this quarter, vs $16.4M in the same quarter a year ago.
footerNote: Reports in thousands, shown in $M. Net income is consolidated, including noncontrolling interests.
